newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds poised to resume the rally.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds poised to resume the rally.

text.p: *Australian bond yields crept above the day's lows by the close in relatively low turnover, but sentiment remains extremely bullish ahead of this week's key data.
Australian bond yields crept above the day's lows by the close in a relative low turnover, but sentiment remains extremely bullish ahead of this week's key data for inflation and wages.

"With the release of inflation and wages data likely to be highly supportive of a monetary easing, we expect the rallying market to continue later this week," said Glenn Maguire, economist at Societe Generale.
Second quarter underlying inflation is forecast to be below the Reserve Bank's 2.0-3.0 percent target and annual wages growth well within the central bank's comfort zone.
Such outcomes to these indicators on Wednesday and Thursday could trigger a further easing in monetary policy, a move that has been largely factored in.
September bill futures' close of 94.90 equates to a cash rate of 5.10 percent and compares with current official interest rates at 5.5 percent.

The market's overall firm tone came in the face of a jittery U.S. Treasury market on Friday ahead of Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's two-day semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testomony, which starts on Tuesday.
Japanese markets were closed on Monday.

Yield spreads to the U.S. narrowed sharply and could test initial support at 25 basis points on the 10-year yield differential if this week's data confirms the benign inflation outlook. And "We now view parity with the U.S. as inevitable," SocGen's Maguire added.

The 10-year bond flirted with initial resistance at 93.470. The contract touched a 3-1/2 year high of 93.510 last week, and where a break could follow through to a test of the all time high of 93.630.
